berberis-thunbergii.title: Address small barberry plants before seed set
berberis-thunbergii.season: Early growing season, before seed set
berberis-thunbergii.detail: Once the identification is confirmed, the reference supports whole-plant pulling for small plants before they set seed. Removing only the tops is not reliable because stump tissue can resprout.

source.label: Penn State Extension · Japanese Barberry

berberis-thunbergii.scope: Pennsylvania management reference; plant stage is more reliable than an assumed NJ date.

berberis-thunbergii.title: Check for persistent red fruit
berberis-thunbergii.detail: Record whether red fruit remains on the shrub during a return visit. The reference describes birds dispersing these seeds, so fruiting is useful context for a confirmed control plan.

source.label: Penn State Extension · Japanese Barberry

berberis-thunbergii.scope: Regional reference phenology, not a verified NJ fruiting calendar.

euonymus-alatus.title: Catch young burning-bush seedlings
euonymus-alatus.season: When young plants are visible; no fixed season supplied
euonymus-alatus.detail: After confirming the species, small infestations can be tackled by hand-pulling young plants. The source distinguishes this from larger established shrubs, which need a different control plan.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

euonymus-alatus.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

euonymus-alatus.title: Use autumn colour and winged stems to refine the match
euonymus-alatus.detail: Photograph the red foliage together with the corky wings on the stems. These source-described features are more useful for checking burning bush than foliage colour alone.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

euonymus-alatus.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

extended-15.title: Remove spent flower stalks
extended-15.detail: For a confirmed plantain lily, cut off the spent flowering stems after blooming. The reference also recommends taking discoloured leaves back to ground level.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

extended-15.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

extended-15.title: Divide only when an established clump needs it
extended-15.season: Early spring before leaves unfurl, or fall
extended-15.detail: The source supports division in spring or fall and notes that early spring, before foliage opens, is easiest. Treat this as an optional care task for an existing confirmed clump, not a reason to spread a non-native plant.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

extended-15.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

buxus-sempervirens.title: Relieve accumulated snow on boxwood
buxus-sempervirens.detail: For an identified boxwood, remove accumulated snow to help protect the branches. Its evergreen foliage and shallow roots also make exposure to drying winter conditions worth noting.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

buxus-sempervirens.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

buxus-sempervirens.title: Thin rather than follow an invented pruning date
buxus-sempervirens.season: Annual pruning decision; avoid very early spring and late summer
buxus-sempervirens.detail: The reference recommends annual thinning for light and airflow but specifically cautions against pruning too early in spring or late in summer. Choose local timing for the confirmed cultivar rather than treating this as a fixed NJ date.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

buxus-sempervirens.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

extended-127.title: Choose whether to extend the flower display
extended-127.season: While flowers are fading during the flowering season
extended-127.detail: For a confirmed black-eyed Susan, optional deadheading can prolong the flowering period. This is a biennial or short-lived perennial, so do not assume each individual clump will persist indefinitely.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

extended-127.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

extended-127.title: Record hairy stems with the flower centre
extended-127.detail: Photograph the short stiff hairs on leaves and stems along with the domed flower centre. These traits help refine the botanical match even while its precise NJ ecological status is unresolved.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

extended-127.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

extended-54.title: Look for a new acorn crop without expecting annual success
extended-54.detail: Track acorn presence and wildlife visits on return scans. Red-oak acorns take two growing seasons to mature, and a young tree can take many years to begin fruiting.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

extended-54.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

extended-54.title: Photograph bristle-tipped leaf lobes
extended-54.detail: Capture a clear leaf showing the pointed, bristle-tipped lobes. The source describes seven to eleven lobes; this offers a more useful identity check than a distant canopy outline.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

extended-54.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

acer-palmatum.title: Check new leaves after frost
acer-palmatum.season: Spring leaf-out and any later frost
acer-palmatum.detail: Record how the new foliage looks after a frost before using damaged leaves to judge identity. The source notes that young Japanese-maple leaves are frost-sensitive.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

acer-palmatum.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

acer-palmatum.title: Check around the parent tree for self-sown plants
acer-palmatum.detail: Look for nearby seedlings and compare their leaves with the parent tree. The source reports that Japanese maple self-seeds readily; an observation is useful before deciding on any control action.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

acer-palmatum.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

hydrangea-macrophylla.title: Check the cultivar before pruning flower-bearing wood
hydrangea-macrophylla.season: Before pruning; especially after the first flush of flowers
hydrangea-macrophylla.detail: For confirmed bigleaf hydrangea, establish whether the cultivar flowers on old wood, new growth, or both before cutting. The source describes old-wood flowering and reblooming cultivars; its North Carolina pruning deadline is not a verified NJ cutoff.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

hydrangea-macrophylla.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

extended-123.title: Identify visitors before treating leaf feeding
extended-123.season: During the growing and flowering season
extended-123.detail: Look for and identify caterpillars before interpreting leaf feeding as a pest problem. Swamp milkweed is a monarch caterpillar host, and the reference says several common milkweed visitors are not problematic.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

extended-123.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

evidence.sourceField: Description · monarch host and common visitors

extended-123.title: Check that this is the moisture-loving milkweed
extended-123.detail: Compare the bed conditions with the reference preference for wet sites or moist clay and loam. Do not assume swamp milkweed has the same dry-soil needs as every other milkweed.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

extended-123.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

solidago-rugosa.title: Keep a late-season flowering record
solidago-rugosa.season: Late summer to fall; exact local timing varies
solidago-rugosa.detail: Photograph the arching yellow flower spikes, upright hairy stems and rough leaves on a late-season visit. Note visiting insects without turning a brief visit into a measured habitat score.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

solidago-rugosa.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

symphyotrichum-novae-angliae.title: Pinch for a bushier aster if desired
symphyotrichum-novae-angliae.detail: For a confirmed New England aster, spring pinching can make the plant bushier. The reference notes that this also delays flowering, so it is an optional shaping choice rather than a required habitat task.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

symphyotrichum-novae-angliae.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

symphyotrichum-novae-angliae.title: Assess support for taller stems
symphyotrichum-novae-angliae.detail: The source notes that taller New England asters may need staking. Check the actual height and stability of the confirmed plant rather than assuming every cultivar needs a stake.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

symphyotrichum-novae-angliae.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

vaccinium-corymbosum.title: Test the soil before a blueberry planting
vaccinium-corymbosum.detail: Use a soil test before establishing highbush blueberry. The source identifies its need for more acidic soil than many other garden plants; do not apply a guessed amendment amount from a photo.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

vaccinium-corymbosum.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

vaccinium-corymbosum.title: Use the establishment-stage pruning window
vaccinium-corymbosum.season: Late winter, from the third year after planting
vaccinium-corymbosum.detail: For a confirmed highbush blueberry that has reached its third year after planting, the reference supports late-winter removal of dead wood and shape maintenance. This is not an instruction to prune a newly planted shrub in the same way.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

vaccinium-corymbosum.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

hedera-helix.title: Separate tree-climbing ivy without pulling it from bark
hedera-helix.season: When confirmed ivy is climbing a tree; no fixed NJ month given
hedera-helix.detail: After confirming English ivy, follow the tree-safe method: sever its connection near ground level and leave the upper growth attached to die. Pulling attached vines from the tree can damage bark. Recheck and cut regrowth as it appears; one cut is not complete control.

source.label: Rutgers Environmental Stewards · English Ivy invasive-species sheet

hedera-helix.scope: NJ Extension guidance; act on confirmed identity and actual tree/site conditions.

hedera-helix.title: Distinguish climbing leaves from mature flowering growth
hedera-helix.season: Early-fall flowering stage in the source reference
hedera-helix.detail: Look for a change from spreading juvenile stems to shrubby flowering growth. The source describes mature stems flowering and later producing berries; leaf shape alone can vary with life stage.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

hedera-helix.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

pyrus-calleryana.title: Use the early white bloom as an identification opportunity
pyrus-calleryana.detail: Photograph the white flower clusters and branch structure while visible. This is a useful time to refine a possible Callery-pear match before planning treatment.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

pyrus-calleryana.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

pyrus-calleryana.title: Focus any simple removal plan on small confirmed seedlings
pyrus-calleryana.season: When seedlings are small and identifiable; no fixed season supplied
pyrus-calleryana.detail: The reference supports hand-pulling or digging seedlings and small trees. This is not a method for a mature tree; choose a separate tree-care plan for established Callery pears.

source.label: Penn State Extension · Pennsylvania’s Newest Noxious Weeds

pyrus-calleryana.scope: Pennsylvania control reference; this record does not assert Pennsylvania legal status applies in NJ.

extended-2.title: Remove the roots of small confirmed privets
extended-2.season: When small plants are identifiable; no calendar window supplied
extended-2.detail: The reference includes border privet among the species it covers. Small plants can be hand-pulled, but remaining roots can resprout; cutting the canopy alone is not reliable control.

source.label: Penn State Extension · The Invasive and Noxious Privet

extended-2.scope: Mid-Atlantic management reference; no verified NJ treatment date is supplied.

extended-2.title: Record both leaf arrangement and the fruit stage
extended-2.season: During flowering or fruiting; source dates are Connecticut-oriented
extended-2.detail: Capture the opposite simple leaves together with white flower panicles or black drupes when present. This helps distinguish a possible border privet from a distant evergreen-shaped shrub.

source.label: University of Connecticut Plant Database

extended-2.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

rosa-multiflora.title: Look for the fringed leaf-base structures
rosa-multiflora.detail: Photograph the fringed stipules at the base of a leaf and any small white flowers. The source identifies these as useful distinctions from other roses and brambles before control is considered.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

rosa-multiflora.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

rosa-multiflora.title: Plan for repeated follow-up, not one clipping
rosa-multiflora.season: Across repeated growing seasons after a confirmed control plan
rosa-multiflora.detail: The reference describes mechanical control as a repeated, multi-year effort. Its mowing schedule is for open pasture settings, not an automatic recommendation for a planted garden bed.

source.label: Penn State Extension · Multiflora Rose Management in Grass Pastures

rosa-multiflora.scope: Pasture-management source; garden-bed methods and local timing need a site-specific plan.

extended-96.title: Remove spent flower clusters and keep shaping light
extended-96.detail: For confirmed mountain laurel, the source recommends removing spent clusters and only light pruning after bloom. Remember that next year’s blossoms develop on old growth.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

extended-96.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

extended-96.title: Keep the shallow root zone cool and moist
extended-96.season: Before and during hot or dry weather
extended-96.detail: The reference recommends mulch to retain moisture and cool the root zone. Compare drainage first: mountain laurel does not perform well in wet or heavy clay soil.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

extended-96.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

cornus-florida.title: Maintain a cooling root-zone mulch layer
cornus-florida.season: Before and during hot summer weather
cornus-florida.detail: For a confirmed flowering dogwood, the source supports a 2–4-inch mulch layer over the root zone to help keep it cool and moist. This does not replace checking drainage and the actual soil moisture.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

cornus-florida.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

cornus-florida.title: Photograph the tiny flowers inside the showy bracts
cornus-florida.detail: The large petal-like parts are bracts around a cluster of small true flowers. A close-up of both helps check the flowering-dogwood match.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

cornus-florida.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

hemerocallis-fulva.title: Watch one flower through its short display
hemerocallis-fulva.detail: Photograph a freshly opened orange flower and revisit it the following day. The source explains that each daylily flower lasts only one day; a faded flower is not, by itself, evidence that the plant is failing.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

hemerocallis-fulva.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

hemerocallis-fulva.title: Track whether the clump is moving beyond its space
hemerocallis-fulva.detail: Record the clump boundary in repeat photos. Orange daylily spreads rapidly by rhizomes, so a boundary record is more useful than assuming every new shoot is a different species.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

hemerocallis-fulva.scope: General horticultural reference; local NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

garden-chelone-glabra.title: Pinch for a bushier turtlehead if desired
garden-chelone-glabra.detail: For a confirmed white turtlehead, the reference supports pinching stem tips in spring for bushier growth. This is optional shaping, not a required habitat task.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

garden-chelone-glabra.scope: General NC State horticultural reference; NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

garden-chelone-glabra.title: Help retain moisture at the root zone
garden-chelone-glabra.detail: The source recommends mulch to retain moisture. Check the existing bed moisture and drainage rather than assuming this moisture-loving plant tolerates a dry site.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

garden-chelone-glabra.scope: General NC State horticultural reference; NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

garden-eupatorium-perfoliatum.title: Watch moisture before interpreting leaf scorch
garden-eupatorium-perfoliatum.detail: Check whether the soil has dried when boneset leaves look scorched. The reference describes a consistent water source and notes that dry soil can scorch foliage; a photo alone cannot identify the cause.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

garden-eupatorium-perfoliatum.scope: General NC State horticultural reference; NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

garden-heliopsis-helianthoides.title: Deadhead if a longer flower display is desired
garden-heliopsis-helianthoides.season: As blooms fade during the flowering season
garden-heliopsis-helianthoides.detail: For a confirmed false sunflower, the source supports removing spent blooms to prolong flowering. This is a display choice; it is not a measured increase in the yard ecosystem score.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

garden-heliopsis-helianthoides.scope: General NC State horticultural reference; NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

garden-veronicastrum-virginicum.title: Consider cutting spent flowers for possible rebloom
garden-veronicastrum-virginicum.detail: For confirmed Culver’s root, the reference recommends cutting spent flowers back to the rosette for possible fall rebloom. Rebloom is a possibility, not a guaranteed NJ result.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

garden-veronicastrum-virginicum.scope: General NC State horticultural reference; NJ timing and cultivar response are not verified.

garden-zizia-aptera.title: Use the basal leaves to refine the golden-alexander match
garden-zizia-aptera.detail: Photograph the simple, heart-shaped basal leaves as well as the yellow flower clusters. The source uses those leaves to distinguish this plant from the similar Zizia aurea.

source.label: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
